extracted.intended_audience: Grade 5 students and elementary classroom teachers (writing instructors)
extracted.subtask_description: A Grade 5 Six Traits rubric set for evaluating student writing in four genres (Narrative, Response to Literature, Expository, Persuasive). For each genre the rubric lists six traits (Ideas, Word Choice, Organization, Sentence Fluency, Voice, Conventions) with level descriptions 6–1 and a scoring-to-percentage guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative — Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The narrator tells about an experience using specific details. The writing keeps the reader’s interest at all times. 5 The writer tells about an experience using many details. The writing keeps the reader’s interest most of the time. 4 The writer tells about an experience but more details are needed. 3 The writer needs to develop the experience. Some details do not relate to the story. 2 The writer needs to focus on the experience. Details are needed. 1 The writer needs to tell about an experience and use details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative — Word Choice
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The writer’s exceptional word choice captures the experience. Figurative language used well. 5 Strong nouns, verbs, and well chosen adverbs and adjectives create vivid, clear pictures. Figurative language is used. 4 Adverbs/adjectives are used. Strong nouns / active verbs would improve sensory images. Figurative language attempted. Some repetition; try synonyms. 3 Strong nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs are needed to create sensory images. No figurative language. Much repetition. 2 General and overused words do not create sensory images. 1 The writer has not considered word choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative — Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The organization makes the essay easy to read. The beginning, middle, and ending work well. Transitions are used. 5 The essay’s beginning, middle, and an ending use some transitions. 4 The middle needs transitions and a paragraph for each main point. 3 The beginning, middle and ending all run together. Paragraphs are needed. 2 The lack of organization is confusing. 1 (not explicitly restated) — organization is missing or confusing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative — Sentence Fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The sentences are skillfully written with few or no errors. 5 (implied strong sentence control) 4 There are some sentence errors. More sentence variety is needed. 3 There are some sentence errors. More sentence variety is needed. 2 The response has many sentence problems. Sentence variety is needed. 1 Sentence construction confuses the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative — Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The writer’s voice sounds confident, knowledgeable, and enthusiastic. 5 The writer’s voice sounds informative and confident. It fits the audience. 4 The writer’s voice sounds well-informed most of the time and fits the audience. 3 The writer sometimes sounds unsure, and the voice needs to fit the audience better. 2 The writer sounds unsure. The voice needs to fit the audience. 1 The writer needs to be aware of the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative — Conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: 4 The response has few or minor errors. Paper shows evidence of proofreading. 3 The response has some errors in punctuation, spelling or grammar. Proofreading is recommended. 2 The response has errors that may confuse the reader. 1 The number of errors confuses the reader and makes the essay hard to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Literature — Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The focus statement, evidence, and related details show real insight into the reading. 5 The response has a clear focus statement, appropriate evidence, and all the necessary details. 4 The response has a clear focus, adequate evidence, but some unnecessary detail needs to be cut. 3 The focus statement is too broad. Cut unnecessary details. Appropriate evidence is needed. 2 The focus statement is not developed. Details and evidence are needed. 1 The response needs a focus statement, details, and evidence from the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Literature — Word Choice
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 Clear word choice creates a response that inspires the reader. 5 Specific nouns and action verbs make the response clear and informative. 4 Some nouns and verbs could be more specific. 3 Too many general words are used. Specific nouns and verbs are needed. 2 General or overused words make this response hard to understand. 1 The writer needs help finding specific words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Literature — Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The organization makes the writing easy to read. 5 The beginning, middle, and ending work well. Transitions are used. 4 The essay’s beginning, middle, and an ending use some transitions. 3 The middle needs transitions and a paragraph for each main point. 2 The beginning, middle and ending all run together. Paragraphs are needed. 1 The lack of organization is confusing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Literature — Sentence Fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: 4 The sentences are skillfully written with few or no errors. 3 There are some sentence errors. More sentence variety is needed. 2 The response has many sentence problems. 1 Sentence variety is needed. Sentence construction confuses the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Literature — Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The writer’s voice sounds confident, knowledgeable, and enthusiastic. 5 The writer’s voice sounds informative and confident. It fits the audience. 4 The writer’s voice sounds well-informed most of the time and fits the audience. 3 The writer sometimes sounds unsure, and the voice needs to fit the audience better. 2 The writer sounds unsure. The voice needs to fit the audience. 1 The writer needs to be aware of the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Literature — Conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: 4 The response has few or minor errors. Paper shows evidence of proofreading. 3 The response has some errors in punctuation, spelling or grammar. Proofreading is recommended. 2 The response has errors that may confuse the reader. 1 The number of errors confuses the reader and makes the essay hard to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository — Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The topic, focus, and details make the essay truly memorable. 5 The essay is informative with a clear focus and specific details. 4 The essay is informative with a clear focus. More specific details are needed. 3 The focus of the essay needs to be clearer, and more specific details are needed. 2 The topic needs to be narrowed or expanded. Many more specific details are needed. 1 The topic is unclear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository — Word Choice
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The word choice makes the essay very clear, informative, and interesting. 5 Specific nouns and action verbs make the essay clear and informative. 4 Some nouns and verbs could be more specific. 3 Too many general nouns are used. Specific nouns and verbs are needed. 2 General or missing words make this essay hard to understand. 1 The writer needs help finding specific words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository — Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The organization makes the writing easy to read. The beginning, middle, and ending work well. 5 Transitions are used. 4 The essay’s beginning, middle, and an ending use some transitions. 3 The middle needs transitions and a paragraph for each main point. 2 The beginning, middle and ending all run together. Paragraphs are needed. 1 The lack of organization is confusing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository — Sentence Fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: 4 The sentences are skillfully written with few or no errors. 3 There are some sentence errors. More sentence variety is needed. 2 The response has many sentence problems. Sentence variety is needed. 1 Sentence construction confuses the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository — Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The writer’s voice sounds confident, knowledgeable, and enthusiastic. 5 The writer’s voice sounds informative and confident. It fits the audience. 4 The writer’s voice sounds well-informed most of the time and fits the audience. 3 The writer sometimes sounds unsure, and the voice needs to fit the audience better. 2 The writer sounds unsure. The voice needs to fit the audience. 1 The writer needs to be aware of the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository — Conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: 4 The response has few or minor errors. Paper shows evidence of proofreading. 3 The response has some errors in punctuation, spelling or grammar. Proofreading is recommended. 2 The response has errors that may confuse the reader. 1 The number of errors confuses the reader and makes the essay hard to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasive — Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The clear reasoning informs and convinces the reader. 5 The essay has a clear opinion statement. Logical reasons support the writer’s opinion. 4 The opinion statement is clear, and most reasons support the writer’s opinion. 3 The opinion statement is clear. Reasons and details are not as complete as they need to be. 2 The opinion statement is unclear. Reasons and details are needed. 1 An opinion statement, reasons, and details are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasive — Word Choice
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 Strong, engaging, positive words contribute to the main message. Every word counts. 5 Strong, positive words help make the message clear. 4 Strong, positive words are used, but some may be too negative. 3 Many words need to be stronger and more positive. 2 The same words are used throughout the essay. 1 Word choice does not communicate the main message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persuasive — Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The organization makes the writing easy to read. 5 The beginning, middle, and ending work well. Transitions are used. 4 The essay’s beginning, middle, and an ending use some transitions. 3 The middle needs transitions and a paragraph for each main point. 2 The beginning, middle and ending all run together. Paragraphs are needed. 1 The lack of organization is confusing.

rubrics_metrics.description: 6 The sentences are skillfully written with few or no errors. 5 (implied strong sentence control) 4 There are some sentence errors. More sentence variety is needed. 3 There are some sentence errors. More sentence variety is needed. 2 The response has many sentence problems. Sentence variety is needed. 1 Sentence construction confuses the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring Guide (32-point scale → percent)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Six Traits scores (each trait 1–6) summed to a maximum of 32 to convert to a percentage per this table; 11 or below is failing.
